item.description:

FFIS is a non-partisan, non-advocacy subscription service that helps states manage the significant share of their budgets that comes from federal sources. FFIS tracks federal budget, legislative, and regulatory actions and translates them into clear, accurate, state-centric analyses for state budget offices, legislative fiscal staff, and others. Qualifications: working knowledge of Medicaid policy, financing, and operations; commitment to accuracy; clear, concise writing for a technical audience; comfort working with data beyond basic spreadsheets; ability to connect detailed program knowledge to the larger fiscal and policy picture; and comfort with presenting and answering questions. Experience on the recipient side of federal funds (state budget office, legislative fiscal agency, state Medicaid or health agency) preferred; experience with dashboards, data visualization, and/or scripting for automation preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $90,000–$115,000. Hybrid (DC area preferred) or remote considered. Generous leave, health insurance, and retirement benefits; FFIS contributes up to 10% of salary to 401(k), including 5% whether or not you contribute. item.description:
A fellowship opportunity is available in the Office of Health Policy within the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in Washington, DC. Note: this is an ORISE-administered fellowship (administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy). Participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or the program administrator -- this is a stipend, not a salary, and there are no employment-related benefits. U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required. A master's or doctoral degree received within the past 5 years is required. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; final deadline December 1, 2026.

The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts who focus on healthcare markets, and will have opportunities to train with a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in both quantitative and qualitative analytical projects in support of ASPE's priorities. Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; and drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points.

Qualifications: a master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field (social science or related) received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects within economics or related fields; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques. The office has particular interest in applicants with experience in demography or actuarial science (not required). U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience; stipend for healthcare benefits (not employer-sponsored benefits). One-year initial appointment, may be renewed contingent on funding. Full-time. Based in Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 (rolling reviews).
